clue.text: Open startling brothel, freely allowing everyone admission

indicators.note: allowing, together with admission, says one piece is let inside the other
admission is the letting-in that puts the word for everyone inside the jumbled letters
freely means the letters of startling brothel are loosely rearranged

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A shocked report on a racy house of ill repute that throws its doors open to all comers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' is the anagram signal; 'allowing ... admission' is the container, with 'everyone' giving ALL. The surface's 'Open' reads as an adjective but is a verb: to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To get proceedings going is to initiate them, the idiomatic sense of open as a verb.

clue.text: Place for waste good to be situated between areas of vegetation — it keeps things clean

indicators.note: to be situated between says the next pieces sit in the middle of the two vegetation words

parts.note: scrub and brush are both areas of low, rough vegetation
a bin is where waste goes

explanation.surface: Instructions for siting a rubbish dump in the undergrowth, oddly praised as hygienic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be situated between' is the container: one leaf gives two words for vegetation, and the bin and good letter sit in the gap where they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff-bristled cleaning tool is described by what it does: it keeps surfaces clean.

clue.text: Finally grasping English, if nothing else

indicators.note: grasping means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: finally means at last

explanation.surface: A grudging remark that someone has eventually got hold of English, which is something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms setting a minimum: whatever else fails, this much holds.

clue.text: The man arranged to acquire Scottish town's rugby ground

indicators.note: to acquire means the jumbled letters take in the next piece
arranged means the letters of the man are put in a new order

parts.note: Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A man fixes things so that some Scottish town gets a rugby stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' gives TENHAM from THE MAN; 'to acquire' puts WICK inside after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Twickenham in south-west London is England's national rugby union stadium, an example of a rugby ground.

clue.text: Leadership, say, blocking border regarding piracy, ultimately

indicators.note: blocking means sitting inside and obstructing the following word

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment
say means for example, abbreviated EG
on means regarding, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of piracy

explanation.surface: Talk of command, say, being used to stop a border crossing in a dispute over piracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example'; 'blocking' is the container and 'ultimately' takes a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance of one state or group over others is a synonym for leadership.

clue.text: Name's held in memory after book from literary family

indicators.note: after says the memory piece follows the book letter in the answer
held in means the name letter goes inside the memory word

parts.note: rote is learning by memory

explanation.surface: Someone's name remembered long after reading a book by a famous writing family.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne made the Yorkshire household of novelist sisters, the best-known writing family.

clue.text: Hide line associated with song

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A songwriter's instruction to tuck a lyric line away beneath the melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a hide is a concealed shelter, as is an animal's den.

clue.text: Ways to secure love in a pitiable state

indicators.note: to secure means the ways enclose and hold the next piece

parts.note: paths are ways
love is zero in tennis, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: Methods for keeping hold of love when one is in a sorry condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality that arouses pity or sorrow, so a near synonym for a pitiable condition.

clue.text: Discourage allowance over punishment? Not initially

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the allowance word above the next piece

parts.note: a discount is an allowance off the price

indicators.note: not initially means the punishment word loses its opening letter

parts.note: penance is self-imposed punishment

explanation.surface: A query whether a reduced punishment might deter people, with a caveat about the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' cuts the P from PENANCE, leaving ENANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To show disapproval of something and so deter it, as a verb meaning discourage.

clue.text: See 1
Folding business? Start finishing early, around morning

indicators.note: around means the shortened word goes round the next piece
finishing early means the start word stops before its last letter

parts.note: origin means start

explanation.surface: A firm going under, told to start shutting early around the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' trims ORIGIN to ORIGI, and 'around' then wraps that shortened word round the morning abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of shaping paper by creasing is literally business with folds.

clue.text: Forger wants money in coin? Hard

indicators.note: in means the next pieces go inside the coin word

parts.note: a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit
wants means lacks
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter who needs funds, pondering a coin and finding it difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter of coins, but means one who works at a forge.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith works metal at a forge, so a literal forger rather than a faker.

clue.text: Smart military leader seizing entry to harbour

indicators.note: seizing means the leader takes hold of the next letter inside

parts.note: CIC stands for commander-in-chief

indicators.note: entry to points to the opening letter of harbour

explanation.surface: A well-dressed general capturing the mouth of a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, the same sense as smart applied to dress.

clue.text: Welsh sign pledge — not something you expect blokes to adopt

definitions.text: not something you expect blokes to adopt

parts.note: an omen is a sign
to swear is to pledge

explanation.surface: A Welshman signs up to a promise that men are unlikely to take on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing sold for women is what men are unlikely to put on, adopting meaning wearing.

clue.text: Keen on turning in? No good chanting

parts.note: into is slang for keen on

indicators.note: turning means the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone who likes going to bed early, judged unsatisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Reciting on a single sustained note is a form of chanting.

clue.text: Part of Japan, hard-working, not quite secure

parts.note: on means working, as with a machine

indicators.note: not quite means the secure word lacks its last letter

parts.note: shut means secure, as a door

explanation.surface: A diligent part of Japan whose security is not quite tight.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of Japan's main islands, so a part of the country.

clue.text: Distribution of American movie format

indicators.note: distribution of means the letters of American are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: The way a US film is distributed, phrased as a format question.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-screen cinema projection system of the 1950s, so a film format.

clue.text: Source of much comment as book is restricted by restraining order

indicators.note: is restricted by means the pieces sit inside the restraining word

parts.note: a gag order restrains speech

explanation.surface: A much-discussed book that a court injunction has kept out of print.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasbag is an over-talkative person, a constant producer of remarks.

clue.text: Stone with offensive smell not likely to be moved

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
olid is an old word for foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A smelly stone that nobody is keen to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: OLID is a rare word meaning rank-smelling, and the clue uses it loosely for the smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive and unemotional, so a stolid person is hard to stir.

clue.text: A main source of support?

parts.note: main is the sea, so a buoyant ring supporting someone at sea; the surface suggests a chief backer

explanation.surface: A question about what chiefly holds something up.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to a person in the water keeps them afloat on the main, the sea.

clue.text: No trace found at sea, conversely

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of no trace are jumbled

explanation.surface: A report that nothing was found after a search at sea, reversing an earlier claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning on the contrary, the same as the other way round.

clue.text: Odd bits of sound study rather unexpected

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first, third and fifth letters of sound

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Strange snatches of noise from the study come as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening quickly and without warning, so unforeseen or surprising.

clue.text: Memory containing zero space

indicators.note: containing means the memory word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A computer memory with no free capacity at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Room is space available, as in no room to move.

clue.text: Men sadly won't appear in New Zealand resort

parts.note: men here are chessmen, and queens are pieces on the board

indicators.note: sadly means the letters of won't are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A lament that no men will be found in a holiday town in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a cryptic definition of a women-only town; in fact 'Men' are chessmen, QUEENS, and 'sadly' rearranges WON'T into TOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Queenstown, on Lake Wakatipu in the South Island, is a well-known adventure and ski resort.

clue.text: End sinks after rising

indicators.note: after rising means in this down clue the sinks word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: sinks as a verb means pots, as of balls in snooker

explanation.surface: A finish that comes once something has floated up, then goes down again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinks' is a verb here: POTS, as in potting a ball in snooker or pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a halt or finish, the noun sense of end.

clue.text: Poorly expressed section, with a bias

parts.note: tilted means leaning, with a bias

explanation.surface: Criticism of a badly written passage that is also slanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted writing is stiff and unnatural, so clumsily phrased.

clue.text: Some have standing regarding exotic scriptures

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people hold authority on matters of foreign holy texts.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for the Avesta, the Zoroastrian sacred texts, and their ancient Iranian language.

clue.text: Relationship arrangement possibly revealing a prior ménage

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of a prior ménage may be put in another order

explanation.surface: A non-exclusive set-up that might hint at an earlier household of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership where both agree to other liaisons is a kind of relationship deal.
